The '''Engel identity''', named after [[Friedrich Engel (mathematician)|Friedrich Engel]], is a mathematical equation that is satisfied by all elements of a [[Lie ring]], in the case of an Engel Lie ring, or by all the elements of a [[group (mathematics)|group]], in the case of an [[Engel group]]. The Engel identity is the defining condition of an [[Engel group]].

== Formal definition ==
A [[Lie ring]] <math>L</math> is defined as a [[nonassociative ring]] with multiplication that is [[anticommutative]] and satisfies the [[Jacobi identity]] with respect to the [[Commutator|Lie bracket]] <math>[x,y]</math>, defined for all elements <math>x,y</math> in the ring <math>L</math>. The Lie ring <math>L</math> is defined to be an n-Engel Lie ring if and only if
* for all <math>x, y</math> in <math>L</math>, the n-Engel identity
<math> [x,[x, \ldots, [x,[x,y]]\ldots]] = 0</math> (n copies of <math>x</math>), is satisfied.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Engel Lie-Algebras|last=Traustason|first=Gunnar|journal=Quart. J. Math. Oxford|year=1993|volume=44|issue=3|pages=355–384|doi=10.1093/qmath/44.3.355}}</ref>

In the case of a [[group (mathematics)|group]] <math>G</math>, in the preceding definition, use the definition {{nowrap|[''x'',''y''] {{=}} ''x''<sup>&minus;1</sup> • ''y''<sup>&minus;1</sup> • ''x'' • ''y''}} and replace <math>0</math> by <math>1</math>, where <math>1</math> is the identity element of the group <math>G</math>.<ref>{{cite web|title=Engel groups (a survey)|author=Traustason, Gunnar|url=http://www.groupsstandrews.org/2009/Talks/Traustason.pdf}}</ref>
